objections.text: The hand-derived five-hit case already includes Tags 'ab' and 'AB' and requires case-insensitive matching. A01 repeats those values with fewer rows and does not attack a different collation path.
objections.resolution: A01 now uses Cyrillic lower-, upper-, and title-case values with nonmatching Cyrillic and accented controls, testing Unicode case folding beyond the ASCII hand-derived inputs.

objections.text: Searching for 'abc' matches Tags 'abc ' both before and after trimming its trailing space, and Tags is not returned in the JSON. The supplied case therefore cannot expose trailing-space loss despite claiming that trap.
objections.resolution: A03 now places the trailing space in SearchText. Its pattern selects values with a space after 'amy' and excludes 'amy' and 'amyx', so trimming the argument changes the result.

objections.text: The hand-derived LIKE '[a-c]' case already supplies matching and non-matching values, including the case-insensitive member 'B', and exercises the same T-SQL character-class translation. A04 is a reduced copy of that attack.
objections.resolution: A04 now sends the reversed range '[c-a]'. That form exercises T-SQL acceptance versus regular-expression invalid-range handling, a mechanism absent from the ordered hand-derived range.

objections.text: The hand-derived LIKE 'a\b' case already supplies 'a\b' and 'ab' and tests that backslash is ordinary in T-SQL LIKE. A05 repeats the same search and rows.
objections.resolution: A05 now ends SearchText with a backslash. A trailing backslash can become a dangling regular-expression escape or escape the appended wildcard, unlike the hand-derived interior backslash.
